answer: A staking bond that vests like sediment turning to shale makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral that only unlocks after sustained useful work, so spinning up a dune of throwaway accounts costs real capital per identity. Honest agents earn reputation that compounds over epochs, while a Sybil swarm must split its stake thinly and cannot fake history. The cost is asymmetric — one genuine oasis of verified work outweighs thousands of cheap copies, because attestation rewards flow to proven contributors, not to sheer numbers.
